verification_principle: Every fetch records URL, timestamp, file size, sha256 hash, and source authority. Derived artifacts (page renders) record the source artifact and the exact derivation parameters so they are independently reproducible. No artifact in this folder may enter the Vernen corpus without a second-mouth countersignature; the provenance record is the substrate that the second mouth verifies against.

fetches.source_authority: California State Assembly, Office of the Chief Clerk — official archive of California session laws
fetches.fetch_method: wget --tries=20 --timeout=60 --continue (initial curl attempts failed mid-transfer; wget --continue resumed and completed)
fetches.content_description: Complete scanned PDF of Volume 1 of Statutes and Amendments to the Codes, Fiftieth Session of the California Legislature, 1933. Contains all chapters of the regular session including Chapter 59 (the Field Act) at printed pages 352–355 (PDF pages 353–356). Image-based PDF with no OCR text layer; pages must be visually rendered for reading.

fetches.source_authority: California State Assembly, Office of the Chief Clerk
fetches.content_description: Index portion (printed pages ~3361–3391) covering A through COURTS. Contains entries pointing to Chapter 59 / printed page 352 for school building construction; entries for earthquake-proof requirements at printed page 1531; entries for public-buildings earthquake reconstruction at printed page 1533.

fetches.source_authority: California State Assembly, Office of the Chief Clerk
fetches.content_description: Cross-reference tables and statutory record appendix (printed pages ~3275–3357), showing additions, amendments, revisions, and repeals affecting the codes and general laws by 1933 legislation. Includes an Agricultural Code cross-reference, Fish and Game Code, Code of Civil Procedure Revision, Military Code, and a Statutory Record section with subsections for Agricultural Code, Civil Code, Code of Civil Procedure, Probate Code, Fish and Game Code, Penal Code, Political Code, School Code, and General Laws. The School Code section (printed page 3347 onward) is the most likely location of the cross-reference for Chapter 59 → School Code, which would document where the Field Act was codified upon enactment.

fetches.derivation_method: pdftoppm -f 353 -l 353 -r 150 -png (renders PDF page 353, which is printed statute page 352, at 150 DPI)
fetches.content_description: First page of Chapter 59 (the Field Act). Shows: 'CHAPTER 59.', the full official title verbatim, the approval line '[Approved by the Governor April 10, 1933. In effect immediately.]', the formula 'The people of the State of California do enact as follows:', Section 1 (vesting authority in Division of Architecture and defining 'school building'), and the beginning of Section 2 (plan approval requirement and fee schedule).
fetches.verification_chain: This image is reproducible from the source PDF by running the stated derivation method. Any party can verify by re-rendering and comparing the resulting hash.

fetches.content_description: Second page of Chapter 59. Shows: Section 2 continued (fee schedule details, Public School Building Fund), Section 3 (invalid contracts), Section 4 (reports requirement).

Third page of Chapter 59. Shows: Section 4 conclusion, Section 5 (rules authority), Section 6 (penalty — felony), Section 7 (inspection authority and duty), Section 8 (inspection of existing buildings on parental request), Section 9 beginning (urgency declaration).

Fourth and final page of Chapter 59. Shows the conclusion of Section 9 (the urgency clause finishing with 'These buildings will be erected, constructed and reconstructed at once and accordingly it is necessary that this act go into immediate effect in order that the lives and property of the people will be protected.'). End of Chapter 59. The page also begins Chapter 60 (an unrelated act amending the California Districts Securities Commission Act), which provides a clean boundary marker confirming Chapter 59 ends here.

fetches.source_authority: California Legislative Information (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), maintained by the Office of Legislative Counsel of California
fetches.source_authority_type: primary (state legislative branch official text repository)
fetches.content_description: Current text of California Education Code section 17280 — the modern codified location for the K-12 school construction supervision requirement that traces back to the 1933 Field Act. Visible amendment history: 'Amended by Stats. 2002, Ch. 33, Sec. 28. Effective April 29, 2002.' Underlying article added by Stats. 1996, Ch. 277, Sec. 3. The full chain from 1933 Ch. 59 to this 1996/2002 codified form is not visible in this single fetch and is outstanding work.

fetches.source_authority: United States Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
fetches.content_description: USGS scientific record of the March 10, 1933 Long Beach earthquake. Establishes the federal scientific consensus on magnitude (M6.4 moment magnitude per Hough and Graves), epicenter (~5 km offshore Huntington Beach), fault (Newport-Inglewood, ~25 km rupture, no surface break), and casualty count (~120 fatalities, primarily from collapse of unreinforced masonry buildings). Notes the earthquake directly prompted the Field Act and California's first statewide seismic building codes.

fetches.source_authority: California Geological Survey, California Department of Conservation
fetches.source_authority_type: primary (state scientific agency for geology and seismology)
fetches.content_description: California Geological Survey's official state record of the 1933 Long Beach earthquake. Provides: date and time (March 10, 1933 at 5:54 PM), magnitude (6.4), epicenter (3 miles south of Huntington Beach, ~8 miles deep), fault (Newport-Inglewood right-lateral strike-slip), casualties (120 deaths total: 52 Long Beach + 17 Compton; ~2/3 hit by debris while fleeing; 500+ injured Long Beach), property damage (~$50M 1933 dollars), and school building damage figures (70 destroyed + 120 damaged = ~75% of schools in the area). Notes: 'Since the enforcement of the Field Act, no school has collapsed because of a seismic event, and there has been no loss of life.'

fetches.source_authority: Division of the State Architect, California Department of General Services
fetches.content_description: Division of the State Architect official 'About' page. Establishes: DSA provides design and construction oversight for K-12 schools, community colleges, and other state-owned/leased facilities; DSA operates under multiple legislative frameworks including Education Code §§ 17280-17316 (K-12) and §§ 81130-81147 (community colleges), Government Code, Health and Safety Code, and Title 24 Regulations Parts 1-12. Headquartered in Sacramento with regional offices in Oakland, Sacramento, Los Angeles, and San Diego. Contains the verbatim operational outcome statement: 'Since the Field Act was enacted in 1933, DSA's review and approval have ensured that there has never been a major structural failure at a public California K-12 school or community college.'
